#!/bin/bash

# Flux directives translated from LSF
# LSF's '-n 8' with a single command is interpreted as a request for 8 cores.
#FLUX: -n 1
#FLUX: -c 8
#FLUX: -t 16:00:00
#FLUX: -g 1
#FLUX: -q amdgpu
#FLUX: -o logs/train_scratch%J.out

#
# --- Omitted LSF options and explanations ---
#
# -M 48000
#   Omitted. This LSF directive sets a per-process memory limit. Flux does not have a
#   direct equivalent in a batch script. More importantly, no total memory reservation
#   was requested.
#   Performance implication: Without an overall memory reservation, the job may be
#   scheduled on a node with insufficient memory, potentially causing it to fail
#   with an out-of-memory error or perform poorly due to heavy swapping.
#
# -R "span[ptile=8]"
#   Omitted. When combined with `-n 8`, this LSF directive ensures all 8 tasks are
#   placed on a single node. This intent is captured by the Flux translation of
#   '-n 1 -c 8', which requests 1 task with 8 cores on one node.
#
# -e logs/train_scratch%J.err
#   Omitted. Flux combines stdout and stderr into the single output file
#   specified by the -o directive. To redirect stderr separately, you can use
#   shell redirection in your command, e.g., 'command 2> ...'.
#

# load modules
module load bedtools/2.29.2-wrl
module load gcc/9.3.0
module load cuda/11.7
module load samtools/1.6-wrl
module load pigz/2.6.0
module load ucsctools
source activate maxatac

# the main command

cd /data/weirauchlab/team/ngun7t/maxatac/runs

maxatac train --genome hg38 \
--arch Transformer_phuc \
--sequence /users/ngun7t/opt/maxatac/data/hg38/hg38.2bit \
--meta_file /data/weirauchlab/team/ngun7t/maxatac/training_data/meta_file.tsv \
--output /data/weirauchlab/team/ngun7t/maxatac/runs/scratch \
--prefix scratch \
--epochs 1

issues: As correctly noted in the script's comments, the original LSF memory limit (`-M 48000`) was omitted. This is a critical omission. Without a memory constraint, the job is at high risk of being scheduled on a node with insufficient memory, leading to an out-of-memory failure, or it could be killed for disrupting other jobs on the node.

The script specifies an output file in a subdirectory (`logs/train_scratch%J.out`) but does not create the `logs` directory. If this directory does not exist in the working directory when the job starts, the job will fail because it cannot create the output file.

The script is extremely non-portable. It uses hardcoded, user-specific absolute paths for the working directory (`/data/weirauchlab/...`) and for multiple command-line arguments. This means the script will only work for one user on one specific system and cannot be easily shared or adapted.
